column1: A Cambridge professor says that a change in drinking habits was the reason for the Industrial Revolution in Britain.
column2: 一位剑桥大学的教授指出，英国工业革命的起因在于饮茶习惯的改变。

column1: Anjana Ahuja reports
column2: 安贾娜·阿胡贾报道

column1: Alan Macfarlane, professor of anthropological science at Kings College, Cambridge, has, like other historians, spent decades wrestling with the enigma of the Industrial Revolution.
column2: 剑桥大学金斯学院的人类学科学教授艾伦·麦克法兰和其他历史学家一样，花费了数十年时间来研究工业革命的奥秘。

column1: Why did this particular Big Bang - the world-changing birth of industry - happen in Britain?
column2: 为什么正是英国发生了这场改变了世界的工业革命呢？

column1: And why did it strike at the end of the 18th century?
column2: 那么，为什么它会在18世纪末出现呢？

column1: Macfarlane compares the puzzle to a combination lock.
column2: 麦克法兰把这个谜题比作一把密码锁。

column1: ‘There are about 20 different factors and all of them need to be present before the revolution can happen,’ he says.
column2: 他说：“大约有二十个不同的因素，必须全部具备，这场革命才有可能发生。”
column5: all of them|所有这些因素
column6: need to be present|必须具备

column1: For industry to take off, there needs to be the technology and power to drive factories, large urban populations to provide cheap labour, easy transport to move goods around, an affluent middle-class willing to buy mass-produced objects, a market-driven economy and a political system that allows this to happen.
column2: 工业要腾飞，需要能让工厂运转的技术和动力，能提供廉价劳动力的庞大城市人口，便于运输货物的交通，愿意购买大批量生产的商品的富裕中产阶级，还需要市场驱动的经济和容许这一切发生的政治体制。
column14: mass-produced objects|大批量生产的商品
column15: market-driven economy|n. 市场驱动的经济

column1: While this was the case for England, other nations, such as Japan, the Netherlands and France also met some of these criteria but were not industrialising.
column2: 虽然这种情况在英国成立，但像日本、荷兰和法国这样的国家也具备部分这些条件，却并未实现工业化。

column1: ‘All these factors must have been necessary but not sufficient to cause the revolution,’ says Macfarlane.
column2: 麦克法兰说：“这些因素一定都是促成这场革命的必要条件，但还不是充分条件。”

column1: ‘After all, Holland had everything except coal, while China also had many of these factors.
column2: 毕竟，荷兰除了煤炭之外，其他条件都具备，而中国也拥有许多类似的资源。

column1: Most historians are convinced there are one or two missing factors that you need to open the lock.’
column2: 大多数历史学家都认为，还缺少一两个关键因素，而这些因素对于解锁这一难题至关重要。

column1: The missing factors, he proposes, are to be found in almost every kitchen cupboard.
column2: 他提出，那些缺失的要素其实几乎可以在每个厨房里找到。

column1: Tea and beer, two of the nation’s favourite drinks, fuelled the revolution.
column2: 茶和啤酒，这两种深受人们喜爱的饮品，为这场革命提供了动力。

column1: The antiseptic properties of tannin, the active ingredient in tea, and of hops in beer - plus the fact that both are made with boiled water - allowed urban communities to flourish at close quarters without succumbing to water-borne diseases such as dysentery.
column2: 茶中的鞣花酸以及啤酒中的啤酒花都具有抗菌特性；而且这两种原料都是用煮沸的水制成的。因此，城市社区能够在如此接近的环境中繁荣发展，而不会受到痢疾等水传播疾病的威胁。

column1: The theory sounds eccentric but once he starts to explain the detective work that went into his deduction, the scepticism gives way to wary admiration.
column2: 这个理论听起来有些古怪，但他一开始解释自己是怎样像侦探一样调查、得出这个结论的，怀疑便逐渐变成了带有几分保留的钦佩。

column1: Macfarlane’s case has been strengthened by support from notable quarters - Roy Porter, the distinguished medical historian, recently wrote a favourable appraisal of his research.
column2: 麦克弗兰的论点因著名人士的支持而得到加强——著名医学史学家罗伊·波特最近撰写了一篇积极的评价，肯定了他的研究。

column1: Macfarlane had wondered for a long time how the Industrial Revolution came about.
column2: 麦克法兰长期以来一直想知道，工业革命究竟是如何发生的。

column1: Historians had alighted on one interesting factor around the mid-18th century that required explanation.
column2: 历史学家们注意到在18世纪中叶有一个值得关注的因素，需要加以解释。

column1: Between about 1650 and 1740, the population in Britain was static.
column2: 大约在1650年至1740年间，英国的人口数量保持不变。

column1: But then there was a burst in population growth.
column2: 但随后人口增长出现了爆发式上升。

column1: Macfarlane says: ‘The infant mortality rate halved in the space of 20 years, and this happened in both rural areas and cities, and across all classes.
column2: 麦克弗兰说：在短短20年的时间里，婴儿死亡率下降了一半，这一变化无论在农村还是城市，也无论在哪个社会阶层都发生了。

column1: People suggested four possible causes.
column2: 人们提出了四个可能的原因。

column1: Was there a sudden change in the viruses and bacteria around?
column2: 周围的病毒和细菌是否发生了突然的变化？

column1: Unlikely.
column2: 不太可能。

column1: Was there a revolution in medical science?
column2: 医学科学有过一场革命吗？

column1: But this was a century before Lister’s revolution.
column2: 但那是在李斯特革命之前一个世纪的事情。

column1: Was there a change in environmental conditions?
column2: 环境状况是否有变化？

column1: There were improvements in agriculture that wiped out malaria, but these were small gains.
column2: 农业上的进步确实消除了疟疾，但这些进展只是微小的提升。

column1: Sanitation did not become widespread until the 19th century.
column2: 直到19世纪，卫生设施才得以广泛普及。

column1: The only option left is food.
column2: 剩下的唯一选择就是食物了。

column1: But the height and weight statistics show a decline.
column2: 但身高和体重的统计数据表明，这些指标出现了下降。

column1: So the food must have got worse.
column2: 因此食物的质量肯定变差了。

column1: Efforts to explain this sudden reduction in child deaths appeared to draw a blank.’
column2: 试图解释儿童死亡率突然下降的现象，似乎未能找到有效解释。

column1: This population burst seemed to happen at just the right time to provide labour for the Industrial Revolution.
column2: 这种人口激增发生的时间恰到好处，为工业革命提供了充足的劳动力支持。

column1: ‘When you start moving towards an industrial revolution, it is economically efficient to have people living close together,’ says Macfarlane.
column2: 麦克法兰说：“社会开始迈向工业革命时，人们集中居住在经济上更有效率。”

column1: ‘But then you get disease, particularly from human waste.’
column2: ‘但那样一来，你就会生病，尤其是因为人类排泄物导致的疾病。’

column1: Some digging around in historical records revealed that there was a change in the incidence of water-borne disease at that time, especially dysentery.
column2: 在历史记录中查证发现，当时水传播疾病的发病率发生了变化，尤其是痢疾。

column1: Macfarlane deduced that whatever the British were drinking must have been important in regulating disease.
column2: 麦克法兰推测，英国人所饮用的某种物质，很可能对于调节疾病有着重要的作用。

column1: He says, ‘We drank beer.
column2: 他说：‘我们喝了啤酒。'

column1: For a long time, the English were protected by the strong antibacterial agent in hops, which were added to help preserve the beer.
column2: 长期以来，英国人依靠啤酒花中含有的强效抗菌成分来保护啤酒。

column1: But in the late 17th century a tax was introduced on malt, the basic ingredient of beer.
column2: 不过，在17世纪末，英国政府开始对麦芽征税，而麦芽是酿造啤酒的基本原料。

column1: The poor turned to water and gin and in the 1720s the mortality rate began to rise again.
column2: 在1720年代，穷人们开始饮用白开水和杜松子酒，导致婴儿死亡率上升。

column1: Then it suddenly dropped again.
column2: 然后价格又突然下降了。

column1: What caused this?’
column2: 这是由什么造成的？

column1: Macfarlane looked to Japan, which was also developing large cities about the same time, and also had no sanitation.
column2: 麦克法兰看着日本，当时日本也在大约同一时期发展出了大型城市，不过日本同样缺乏卫生设施。

column1: Water-borne diseases had a much looser grip on the Japanese population than those in Britain.
column2: 由水传播的疾病对日本人的影响远小于对英国人的影响。

column1: Could it be the prevalence of tea in their culture?
column2: 难道是因为茶在他们的文化中非常流行吗？

column1: Macfarlane then noted that the history of tea in Britain provided an extraordinary coincidence of dates.
column2: 麦克法兰随后指出，英国茶叶发展史中存在一些日期上的巧合。

column1: Tea was relatively expensive until Britain started a direct clipper trade with China in the early 18th century.
column2: 在18世纪初英国开始与中国进行直接茶叶贸易之前，茶叶一直相对昂贵。

column1: By the 1740s, about the time that infant mortality was dipping, the drink was common.
column2: 到了18世纪40年代，随着婴儿死亡率下降，茶饮在英国变得十分普遍。

column1: Macfarlane guessed that the fact that water had to be boiled, together with the stomach-purifying properties of tea meant that the breast milk provided by mothers was healthier than it had ever been.
column2: 麦克法兰推测，由于水需要煮沸，再加上茶具有清洁肠胃的功效，因此母亲分泌的母乳比以往任何时候都更加健康。

column1: No other European nation sipped tea like the British, which, by Macfarlane’s logic, pushed these other countries out of contention for the revolution.
column2: 没有其他欧洲国家像英国人那样啜饮茶，按照麦克弗莱的逻辑，正是这种习惯使得其他国家无法参与工业革命的竞争。

column1: But, if tea is a factor in the combination lock, why didn’t Japan forge ahead in a tea-soaked industrial revolution of its own?
column2: 但是，如果茶是组合锁中的一个关键因素，为什么日本就未能自行推动一场以茶为特色的工业革命呢？

column1: Macfarlane notes that even though 17th-century Japan had large cities, high literacy rates, even a futures market, it had turned its back on the essence of any work-based revolution by giving up labour-saving devices such as animals, afraid that they would put people out of work.
column2: 麦克法兰指出，尽管十七世纪的日本有大城市、很高的识字率，甚至还有期货市场，它却背离了任何生产变革的要义。日本放弃了畜力等节省劳力的手段，担心这些手段会让人失业。
column13: put people out of work|使人失业

column1: So, the nation that we now think of as one of the most technologically advanced entered the 19th century having ‘abandoned the wheel’.
column2: 因此，我们如今认为在技术上最为先进的国家，在进入19世纪时却已经‘放弃了使用轮子’。
